Notes from mixing Kirsty Duncan's EP "Low Tide Hymns" (5 tracks, finished November 2024) in the box room. The room and mics are in [[Home recording setup]]; this is what I do to a lead voice once it's recorded.

## Tracking first

Kirsty sang into the SM7B through the Cloudlifter, about 8 cm from the grille, pop filter, no compression on the way in. Gain staged so peaks hit around -10 dBFS in Reaper. Three full takes per song plus drop-ins, then comp. Comping took longer than the mix on "Saltcoats" (track 3).

## The chain, in order

1. Clip gain to even out phrases before anything else. Saves the compressor a lot of work.
2. High-pass at 90 Hz, 12 dB/oct. On her lower songs, 75 Hz.
3. Subtractive EQ: a narrow cut at 340 Hz, about -3 dB, for the boxy SM7B thing. In my room the boxiness is half the mic and half the room.
4. De-esser at 6.8 kHz. Her esses are sharp and the TLM 102 made them worse, which is why we switched mics on day two.
5. Opto compressor (LA-2A style), 4 to 5 dB gain reduction, slow and smooth.
6. FET compressor (1176 style), 4:1, fast attack, only catching the peaks, 2 to 3 dB.
7. Gentle air shelf, +2 dB from 10 kHz.

## Space

- Plate reverb, 1.8 s decay, 40 ms pre-delay, high-passed at 300 Hz so it doesn't muddy the guitars.
- Dotted eighth delay synced to the song. "Saltcoats" is 104 BPM, so 433 ms. Delay return filtered hard, 400 Hz to 4 kHz.
- On the ballad "Ardrossan Light" (68 BPM), no delay at all, just a short room reverb, 0.9 s. Felt more honest.

## Rides and automation

Volume rides by hand for the last chorus of every track. Plugins can't tell when a line matters. About 45 minutes per song on automation alone. Breaths: turned down 6 dB, not removed. Removing them makes her sound like a robot.

## Level and loudness

Masters land around -14 LUFS integrated, true peak -1 dBTP, for streaming. Reference tracks: Julie Byrne "Natural Blue" (2017) for space, Big Thief "Not" (2019) for how loud a voice can sit against guitars.

## Mistakes and fixes

- First mix of "Saltcoats" had the vocal 2 dB too loud. Checked on the car stereo and Kirsty's phone. Turned it down.
- Used a pitch corrector on one held note in track 5 and it warbled. Nudged it by hand instead, 18 cents.
- Bounced at 44.1 kHz by mistake once, sent the wrong files to the mastering engineer (Neil Paterson, invoice NP-2208, £250 for five tracks). He spotted it.

## Billing

Charged Kirsty £600 for the mix, £120 per track, which is cheap. Tracked in the [[Budget spreadsheet]]. Related: [[Sound design]] for the film side of reverb thinking.
